tells.1: The fabric-compatibility check comes after the application step it should precede, a sequencing slip typical of assembled text. Otherwise the phrasing is uniformly formal ("is compatible with," "exposing it to rain").
tells.3: The "Got a leaky tent seam? It's an easy fix." hook feels bolted on. "Before you start, double-check" appears mid-procedure, after the application step.
tells.5: Word-for-word identical to version 1 apart from straight vs. curly apostrophes. It has the same misplaced compatibility check and the same stiff, uniform cadence.

reason: Versions 2 and 4 put the compatibility check before application and read cleanly. Version 4 has the most natural editorial rhythm, but version 2 keeps the topic-framing opening and fits the single-paragraph format, so it's the one I'd publish.
